questions.q: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y = \frac{x+1}{x-2}$ at the point $(3, 4)$.
questions.explain: Use the quotient rule to find the gradient $\frac{dy}{dx}$: let $u = x+1$, $v = x-2$. $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{(1)(x-2) - (1)(x+1)}{(x-2)^2} = \frac{-3}{(x-2)^2}$. At $x=3$, gradient $m = \frac{-3}{1^2} = -3$. The equation is $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1) \implies y - 4 = -3(x - 3) \implies y - 4 = -3x + 9$, which rearranges to $3x + y - 13 = 0$.
